summary: QRU Automated Pre-Review Inspection™ + Product Family Manufacturing™ end-to-end verified. Backend: 10/10 pytest tests passed against the deployed preview backend. GET /api/book-mfg/books/{id}/inspection returns the correct read-only exception report shape {summary:{clean,blocking,recommended,advisory,total_exceptions,publish_ready}, exceptions[], founder_judgment[], read_only:true, never_rewrites:true, product:{...}} for both BOOK-0013 and BOOK-0018 — content and word-count are byte-identical before vs after inspection (read-only verified). BOOK-0018 has NO content_integrity finding (proves the KR-00080 rebuild is correctly authored). GET /api/family/intents returns exactly 6 intents (consumer, classroom, homeschool, professional, corporate, exam_prep) + available_families. GET /api/family/eligible-sources returns 18 sources including DEC-00018 in review_state='Founder Approved' (eligibility fix confirmed — states above 'Manufacturing Ready' are now included). GET /api/family/preview?decoder_id=DEC-00018&intent=consumer → source.eligible=true, gate.match.level='ok', can_manufacture=true. POST /api/family/assemble with DEC-GATETEST returns HTTP 409 detail.error='source_verification_failed' + gate.match.level='critical' (source gate still blocks). FAM-5EA08F8F verified in /api/family/history with 3 ok items — BOOK-0018 (Book), PRD-00240 (Workbook), PRD-00241 (Teacher Guide) — all linked to KR-00080. FRONTEND: logged in as demo.admin@qru.com. (1) /product-family loads (data-testid=product-family-page). Source select has 19 options (18 sources + placeholder). Selecting DEC-00018 + intent-consumer shows family-preview-panel with family-gate-verdict='Source matches the subject / Consumer / General reader' and 1 pre-checked family-check-Book; assemble-family-btn present and enabled. Switching to intent-classroom shows 3 pre-checked chips: family-check-Book, family-check-Workbook, family-check-Teacher-Guide. Switching source to DEC-GATETEST turns family-gate-verdict red 'Mismatch — manufacturing blocked' and disables the assemble button. assemble-family-btn was intentionally NOT clicked (Founder cost-sensitive; FAM-5EA08F8F already exists). (2) /book-manufacturing?book=<BOOK-0018-uuid> renders preview-inspection-panel with 'Automated Pre-Review Inspection™' heading; clicking run-inspection-btn produces inspection-report with severity chips: inspection-blocking=0, inspection-recommended=1, inspection-advisory=2, and 'No blocking issues — publish-ready' badge. Three inspection-exc-* items are visible: inspection-exc-structure (12 chapters look nearly empty), inspection-exc-frontmatter (no copyright line), inspection-exc-spelling (1 unrecognized word). Toast 'X exception(s) flagged for your review.' shown. Verified in backend test that content/word-count are unchanged after inspection — no rewrite.

minor.issue: get_book (router) only accepts UUID id, not book_code — inconsistent with the inspection endpoint which accepts both. Not blocking; only affects code-based lookups. Consider adding {'$or':[{'id':id},{'book_code':id}]} for consistency.

PRD-00240 and PRD-00241 return 404 when queried by product_code (only accessible by UUID). Non-blocking — the family history record correctly reports both PRD codes. Consider allowing lookup by product_code.

issues: Console hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>'. This is caused by the Emergent visual-editor injecting <span x-excluded=true> wrappers around the option label; it does not break the app but produces a benign React DOM validation warning in dev builds. Non-blocking.

action_items: OPTIONAL: allow GET /api/book-mfg/books/{id} to accept book_code as well as UUID (align with inspection endpoint).
OPTIONAL: allow GET /api/products/{code} to accept product_code (PRD-*) as well as UUID.
critical_code_review_comments: preflight_inspection.py: correctly enforces read-only — inspect_book only reads from db.book_records and inspect_document is pure. NEVER writes back. Constitutional rule preserved.
family_assembly.assemble: correctly gates on gate.match.level=='critical' before entering the family loop; override flag is Founder-only via require_super_admin. Good.
family_assembly.assemble catches per-family exceptions with try/except and reports them as {ok:false,error} rather than blowing up the whole family. Good defensive design.
routers/family.py history endpoint uses get_current_user (any authenticated user) — consider whether product-family history should be super_admin-only in production. Non-blocking.
family_assembly._build_family_package uses re_engine._save which is a private-ish underscore-prefixed helper — consider exposing a public alias for maintainability. Minor.

Console hydration warning about <span> in <option> is caused by the visual-editor injecting x-excluded spans; consider suppressing at build time for /product-family since it produces a noisy React DOM warning. Cosmetic.
